chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) used to say: 'All people are free, except for one who acknowledges slavery upon himself while he is mature, from a male or female slave, and whoever is testified against with slavery, whether he be young or old.'
ai.seo_question: What is the default legal status of humans in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *al-asl al-hurriyyah* (the default state of freedom), a cornerstone of Shia fiqh where slavery is considered an exception requiring proof. It specifies that emancipation is the norm unless an individual is explicitly recognized as a slave, a status applicable to both males and females regardless of age at the time of testimony. This hadith underscores the legal presumption of liberty, limiting the scope of enslavement to those with clear, acknowledged status.
